evidence.source: 中央研究院小學堂文字學資料庫
evidence.text: The entry groups 肉 forms under oracle-bone script, Chu bamboo-and-silk, and Small Seal categories, and explains the ancient graph as shaped like a piece of meat. It does not provide dates for individual specimens or a full sequence of graphic changes.
evidence.title: 漢字「肉」：字形演變

evidence.text: The source describes 肉 in oracle-bone forms as a graph shaped like animal flesh. This supports the pictographic analysis; the page also discusses how the graph may become visually confusable with 月 in later forms, but does not date the individual 肉 specimens on the inspected page.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：肉

evidence.text: The received Shuowen text reads 胾肉。象形。凡肉之屬皆从肉。 Duan Yucai interprets 胾 as a large piece of animal meat and describes uses extended to the ring-body sense in 爾雅肉好 and the musical usage 廉肉. These are historical dictionary claims, not dated attestations of the extensions.
evidence.kind: historical dictionary text and later annotation
evidence.title: 說文解字「肉」

evidence.text: The entry cites meat usage in 左傳·隱公元年 and 孟子·梁惠王上, and bodily flesh in 荀子·正論, 墨子·節葬, and 戰國策·趙策. It separately cites fruit pulp in 齊民要術·種竹, musical voice in 禮記·樂記, and the solid part of a perforated ring in 爾雅·釋器 and 漢書·食貨志 commentary. The entry supplies citations but does not establish their exact wording dates or the earliest attestation of each sense.
evidence.title: 肉 ròu - 漢典

evidence.text: The entry gives Middle Chinese as 日母 屋韻 入聲, 如六切, and reports Old Chinese labels in the Huang Kan and Wang Li systems without a single shared transcription. A supplied local Baxter–Sagart 2014 row records 肉 MC nyuwk and OC *k.nuk; a supplied local Unihan row records kMandarin ròu. These local rows were not independently verified against the official Unicode character page, which was inaccessible during this research.
evidence.kind: pronunciation metadata with local row provenance
evidence.title: 肉 ròu - 漢典

evidence.text: The exact file page identifies Shuowen Seal Radical 135.svg as a Lesser Seal graph and one of the 540 Shuowen radicals. The file is uploader LiliCharlie’s own work, dated 9 December 2013, manually straightened in Inkscape, and licensed CC BY-SA 3.0. It is a modern redraw of a seal-script form, not a photograph or ancient specimen.

search_audit.outcome: Official Unihan lookup and alternate query were inaccessible; ZIP was rejected by the browser as unsupported content type. Search results did not establish a primary source for proposed deep Proto-Sino-Tibetan etymologies. Local row data remains explicitly local.

gaps: No inspected primary source establishes dates for individual 肉 oracle-bone, Chu manuscript, or seal specimens, nor a complete sequence of graphic changes. The seal glyph selected here is explicitly a modern redraw, not an artifact image.

Dictionary citations preserve early-looking meat and bodily-flesh examples, but exact composition dates, transmission history, and earliest attestations for meat, bodily flesh, fruit pulp, musical voice, and ring-body senses remain unverified. Do not infer a chronology from the dictionary’s sense order.

No inspected primary source resolves the dossier’s competing deeper word-etymology proposals (Proto-Sino-Tibetan *now ‘tender/soft’ versus *s-nja-k ‘meat/flesh’). The graph’s pictographic analysis does not settle the spoken word’s deeper origin; these proposals remain unverified.

Official Unicode Unihan record requests for U+8089 were inaccessible in this session. Supplied local kMandarin and Baxter–Sagart rows are reported as local data only; no external click-through confirmation was obtained.
Commons file page records a redraw derived from the Shuowen Small Seal form, but it does not identify a photographed source exemplar or an archaeological date for the model.

items.period: Modern redraw published 2013; represents the Shuowen Small Seal tradition
items.caption: A modern, manually straightened redraw of the Shuowen Small Seal form of 肉. It illustrates the seal-script tradition used for the pictograph; it is not an excavated ancient specimen.
items.alt: A modern line drawing of the 肉 Small Seal form, with an outer meat-like outline and interior strokes.
items.selection_reason: The Commons description page verifies that this is the Small Seal radical form of 肉, supplies its original SVG URL, and provides CC BY-SA 3.0 rights. It can illustrate the seal-script category reported by the Academia Sinica evolution record, while its modern-redraw status is made explicit.

limitations.text: This candidate is a 2013 modern redraw manually straightened in Inkscape, not an ancient artifact photograph. Inspected paleographic text supports the pictographic interpretation and script category but does not date a specific seal specimen or establish a detailed chronological sequence.
